titre: The Flood That Invented Art Restoration
accroche: On November 4, 1966, water covers the head of the Christ painted by Cimabue in Florence, and volunteers from around the world rush in.
contenu_vulgarise:
## The Water Rises

On November 4, 1966, before dawn, the Arno overflows into Florence. In a few hours, water floods the narrow streets of the historic center, rising to five or six meters in places. In the refectory of the basilica of Santa Croce, the great Crucifix painted by Cimabue around 1288 stays submerged for several hours, the head of Christ disappearing under the mud. When the water recedes, nearly 60% of its paint layer has come away from the wood with it. A few streets away, the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale sees its basement and ground floor swallowed up: nearly a million books, newspapers and manuscripts soak in mud mixed with fuel oil.

## The Improvised Rescue

No institution is ready for a disaster of this size. The Gabinetto del Restauro of the Florentine Superintendency, an existing restoration laboratory, has never had to treat tens of thousands of waterlogged volumes at once. In the days that follow, volunteers pour in from Florence, then from Italy, then from at least thirty or so countries: students, chemists, bookbinders, professional restorers. The local press soon nicknames them the *angeli del fango*, the mud angels. They form chains to pass the books out hand to hand, dry them in tobacco-drying sheds for lack of anything better, and spread them out on every available floor in the city. The emergency forces them to invent on the spot: no one yet knows how to stabilize so much sodden paper without destroying it further.

## A Discipline Born of Emergency

It is this forced improvisation that turns into method. The British bookbinder Peter Waters, who came to lend a hand, develops with his colleagues the freeze-drying of books, a technique borrowed from the food industry to dry them without warping them, and “phased conservation”: stabilize first in the emergency, restore in detail later, when time allows. Back in the United States, he will go on to create the Library of Congress's conservation office. In Florence itself, Cimabue's Crucifix is entrusted to Umberto Baldini and Ornella Casazza, who invent a new technique for its gaps in the paint, chromatic abstraction: fine vertical colored hatchings, visible up close but blending together at a distance, never an overpainting that would create an illusion. The project lasts ten years.

The Florentine restoration laboratory, overwhelmed, moves into the larger premises of the Fortezza da Basso. In 1975, it merges with the former Opificio delle Pietre Dure, a Medici workshop of the 16th century, to form the institute that bears that name today and remains a global reference in restoration. What the flood produced in the emergency (documented phases of treatment, reversible materials, international cooperation among professionals) remains the basic grammar of the trade.

carte.punch: In 1966, a flood of the Arno forces people to invent restoration methods on the spot.
carte.idee: On November 4, 1966, the Arno floods Florence: nearly a million books from the Biblioteca Nazionale and Cimabue's Crucifix are submerged. Volunteers from at least thirty or so countries improvise the rescue; the freeze-drying of books and phased conservation are born of it.

quiz.question: Why did the 1966 Florence flood advance art restoration as a scientific discipline?
choix: Because UNESCO financed the construction of a new museum to replace the lost works
Because Cimabue had left written instructions on how to restore his work
Because the Italian state banned the display of any work not restored after the flood
Because the scale of the damage forced restorers to invent, in an emergency, techniques still used today
quiz.explication: No institution was equipped for a disaster of this scale: the freeze-drying of books, phased conservation and chromatic abstraction were born of this emergency, not of a pre-established plan.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who develops the freeze-drying of books and phased conservation during the 1966 rescue?
choix: The Italian government, by emergency decree
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text names Peter Waters as the author of these two techniques; Baldini and Casazza, for their part, invented chromatic abstraction for Cimabue's Crucifix, a different technique.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What technique do Baldini and Casazza invent to restore the gaps in the paint of Cimabue's Crucifix?
choix: An exact overpainting, invisible to the naked eye
Replacing the lost areas with photographs
Fine colored hatchings that blend together at a distance, never an overpainting
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text describes chromatic abstraction as fine vertical colored hatchings, visible up close but blending together at a distance, never an overpainting that would create an illusion.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In what year does the Florentine restoration laboratory merge with the former Opificio delle Pietre Dure?
choix: 1966, the same year as the flood
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that the merger with the former Opificio delle Pietre Dure, a Medici workshop of the 16th century, takes place in 1975, nine years after the flood of 1966.
